skill.name: youtube-thumbnail-design
skill.description: Design YouTube thumbnails using proven dimensions, safe zones, contrast, concise text, expressive subjects, mobile previews, generation prompts, and controlled A/B tests.
skill.summary: Create clear, high-contrast YouTube thumbnails that remain readable on mobile.
skill.author: 101-skills

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are Markdown backticks or design prose, not executable reconnaissance. Confirmed risks are documented npx and belt workflows, mutable external install guidance, and prompt transmission to inference.sh. No prompt injection, secret access, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: The skill asks agents to install packages and run an authenticated third-party CLI.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation, pin installable dependencies, and verify package sources before installation or execution.

remediation.issue: Image prompts are transmitted to inference.sh applications.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose the external data transfer and warn users not to include confidential, personal, or regulated information.

content.value_statement: Weak thumbnails lose clicks before viewers evaluate the video. This skill provides layout rules, generation prompts, mobile checks, and testing guidance for stronger designs.
actual_capabilities: Defines thumbnail dimensions, aspect ratio, file-size limits, and supported image formats.
Applies a 120-pixel mobile readability test and identifies unsafe overlay zones.
Recommends contrast pairs, text limits, subject placement, and facial expressions.
Provides belt CLI prompt examples for common thumbnail formats and content types.
Structures single-variable A/B tests and supplies a practical review checklist.
limitations: Image generation requires the belt CLI, an inference.sh account, and network access.
The skill does not perform image editing, typography placement, or file compression by itself.
Design recommendations are heuristics and cannot guarantee higher click-through rates.
External application names, commands, pricing, and availability may change.

use_cases.title: Plan a Creator Thumbnail
use_cases.description: Turn a video topic into a focused composition, short text concept, color pair, and generation prompt.

use_cases.title: Standardize Channel Reviews
use_cases.description: Evaluate thumbnails against mobile readability, safe zones, contrast, brand consistency, and content accuracy.

use_cases.title: Prepare Controlled Tests
use_cases.description: Create paired thumbnail concepts that change one variable while preserving the remaining design.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Concept
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a YouTube thumbnail concept for [video topic]. Suggest one focal subject, one color pair, optional text under six words, and a mobile-safe layout.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when starting from a video topic.

prompt_templates.title: Write an Image Prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Write an image-generation prompt for [video topic] at 16:9. Include composition, expression, lighting, contrast, background, subject placement, and empty space for text.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when preparing an AI-generated base image.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Existing Thumbnail
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this thumbnail description: [description]. Check the 120-pixel test, safe zones, contrast, text length, focal hierarchy, accuracy, and likely mobile readability.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before publishing or revising a design.

prompt_templates.title: Build an A/B Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Create two thumbnail briefs for [video]. Change only [test variable]. Keep subject, framing, text, branding, and visual complexity consistent. Explain the measurement plan.

output_examples.input: Create a thumbnail concept for a beginner video about fixing slow laptops.
output: Subject: concerned creator beside a slow laptop icon.
Layout: face left, laptop center, text upper right.

output_examples.input: Review a thumbnail with eight small words and a product in the bottom-right corner.
output_examples.output: Reduce the text to six words or fewer. Move the product away from the duration overlay and increase subject contrast.

output_examples.input: Plan a test comparing a bright background with a dark background.
output: Variant A uses a bright yellow background.
Variant B uses a dark navy background.
Keep the face, text, crop, and subject placement unchanged.
Compare click-through rate over equivalent audience samples.

best_practices: Preview every design at approximately 120 pixels before approval.
Keep one dominant focal point and reserve overlay-safe space near the lower corners.
Test one variable at a time and match every thumbnail to the actual video.
anti_patterns: Do not repeat the full video title in small thumbnail text.
Do not place important subjects beneath duration, chapter, or progress overlays.
Do not compare test variants that change multiple visual variables simultaneously.

faq.question: What thumbnail size does the skill recommend?
faq.answer: Use at least 1280 by 720 pixels with a 16:9 aspect ratio. The guide also recommends 1920 by 1080 pixels.

faq.question: Does this skill generate images directly?
faq.answer: It provides belt CLI examples for inference.sh applications. Generation requires the external CLI, an account, and network access.

faq.question: How much text should a thumbnail contain?
faq.answer: Use no more than six words. Choose bold text that remains readable in a 120-pixel mobile preview.

faq.question: Can the skill guarantee a higher click-through rate?
faq.answer: No. It provides design heuristics and testing methods, but performance depends on audience, topic, title, competition, and distribution.

faq.question: How should I run an A/B test?
faq.answer: Change one variable between variants. Keep composition, subject, text, and branding stable, then compare equivalent audience samples.

faq.question: What information should I avoid sending to image services?
faq.answer: Do not include confidential plans, personal data, credentials, regulated information, or unpublished client material in external prompts.
